definition: AI used to detect or prevent fraud, screen transactions (sanctions/AML) and run know-your-customer due diligence.
include_rules: Fraud scoring or prediction; transaction or sanctions screening; AML alert triage; KYC/client due-diligence checks; identity verification done BY the firm with AI.
exclude_rules: AI-enabled attacks or identity fraud BY criminals (-> C12 risk). Speed or experience of account opening without a KYC/screening angle (-> C06). Cyber-defence with no fraud angle (no category yet - note it).
example_paraphrase: [1] The investment bank says AI has let it handle over twice as many transaction-screening reviews while cutting manual operator checks by half. [2] AI/ML in KYC work is credited with cutting unit costs by close to 40%, and with cheaper, more effective sanctions screening and fraud protection. [3] The consumer bank says its AI work started in risk areas such as fraud detection more than ten years ago.

definition: AI used in deciding whether, how much and at what terms to lend (consumer, mortgage, card, commercial).
include_rules: Underwriting models; credit decisioning; loan-origination AI; credit-line or pricing decisions on loans.
exclude_rules: 'Automatically decisioned' applications with no AI term in the passage (rules engines are not AI unless stated). Credit-RISK measurement of the existing book (-> C03). Insurance underwriting (no evidence in banks; add a sub-tag if insurers join).
example_paraphrase: [1] The consumer bank says it applies data and AI-enabled techniques to refine underwriting and credit decisions across its mortgage business. [2] Home Lending ties its spending on technology, data and AI to better sales and underwriting and faster time to market. [3] The consumer bank describes predictive AI/ML in credit as a mature, established use case.

definition: AI/ML used to measure, monitor or manage the firm's own market, credit, liquidity or operational risk, incl. valuation and stress-testing models and 'risk intelligence'.
include_rules: Risk measurement and stress testing with ML; model-risk frameworks that state the firm uses ML/AI models; AI that flags operational or control issues early.
exclude_rules: Risks CAUSED BY AI (bias, AI failures, AI regulation -> C12). Fraud and screening (-> C01). Credit decisions on new loans (-> C02).
example_paraphrase: [1] The 10-K's model-risk section says the firm uses estimation models, some built on ML or AI, across businesses for valuation, risk measurement, capital and stress tests. [2] The pay narrative for a senior executive credits AI and ML with improving workflows and risk intelligence. [3] Asset & Wealth Management says it uses AI in part to streamline processing and manage risk, alongside routine stress testing of client portfolios.

definition: AI used in trading, pricing, securities inventory, execution or optimizing the trading balance sheet and capital.
include_rules: Algorithmic or AI-assisted trading and execution; pricing; securities-financing inventory; capital/balance-sheet optimization in Markets.
exclude_rules: Client-facing recommendations from Markets data (-> C05). 'Algorithmic trading' with no AI term nearby (not AI unless stated). Research reports (-> C10).
example_paraphrase: [1] The 2023 letter says Prime Finance was starting to apply AI to manage the securities inventory held for clients while using the balance sheet more efficiently. [2] By 2025 Prime Finance is described as using AI for inventory, sharper pricing, risk and capital efficiency. [3] Listed AI use cases include tools that optimize how capital is used in the trading business.

definition: AI that decides or suggests what to offer or recommend to clients - delivered straight to clients (personalization, robo-advice, marketing) or through advisors and bankers (next-best-action and prospecting tools).
include_rules: Personalized offers and experiences; marketing targeting; pricing of products for customers; robo-advice; advisor/banker tools that surface client opportunities, prepare meetings or suggest ideas (e.g. Connect Coach, Sales Assist).
exclude_rules: Servicing an existing request (-> C06). Investment research for portfolio managers (-> C10). General employee GenAI tools not aimed at selling/advising (-> C09).

[2] Connect Coach reportedly reaches about 12,000 advisors with 25 specialized AI agents, pushing roughly a million tailored insights to help prospect and prepare client meetings. [3] The consumer bank says its AI focus moved from cutting cost and risk toward revenue growth, with data used to personalize at scale.

definition: AI used to serve clients' existing needs: contact-centre support, routing, faster onboarding, and AI features inside tools clients use themselves (e.g. cash-flow forecasting).
include_rules: Chatbots / virtual assistants for customers; call prediction and routing; agent-assist in service; onboarding speed and experience; AI features in client treasury or banking tools.
exclude_rules: KYC/screening checks during onboarding (-> C01). Tools that recommend products (-> C05). Internal employee assistants (-> C09).
example_paraphrase: [1] Service specialists are said to be supported by AI for predicting calls, giving real-time insights and routing calls intelligently. [2] The commercial bank says it already applies AI to bring customers on board faster and to give clients more insight. [3] Corporate treasury clients are said to have a cash-flow-forecasting tool to help manage liquidity.

exclude_rules: Automation with NO AI term in the passage (RPA, 'automated' rules - not AI). Screening/KYC operations (-> C01). Software development (-> C08).

[3] AWM mentions applying AI to streamline trade, transaction and money-movement processing.

definition: General-purpose AI given to employees (LLM platforms, assistants, knowledge search, drafting/summarizing), plus AI used in HR processes such as training or recruiting.
include_rules: Enterprise GenAI/LLM platforms (e.g. LLM Suite); employee assistants and agents; knowledge tools; AI-delivered training (e.g. role plays); recruiting with AI.
exclude_rules: Training employees ABOUT AI or hiring AI talent (-> C11: building capability, not using AI). Coding tools (-> C08). Tools whose purpose is selling/advising clients (-> C05).
example_paraphrase: [1] The firm says it gave its in-house generative AI platform, LLM Suite, to over 200,000 staff in 2024, inside a controlled environment that protects data. [2] The firm says it recently launched an AI-powered Employee Assistant agent as a single place for staff to get help and complete tasks. [3] Private-bank advisor training now uses AI-driven role plays; practice volume rose while cost per advisor trained fell by about a quarter.

definition: Text about risks created by AI (failures, bias, misuse, AI-enabled attacks, workforce displacement, competition), AI regulation, and how the board and management oversee AI.
include_rules: Risk factors about AI; AI-enabled cyber or identity attacks by others; AI regulation; board/committee oversight of AI; director AI expertise; shareholder engagement on AI; responsible-AI controls.
exclude_rules: The firm USING AI to manage risk (-> C03) or fight fraud (-> C01).
example_paraphrase: [1] The 2024 risk factors warn that biased or misleading AI output could cause harm such as discriminatory lending, fraud or privacy breaches, damaging reputation. [2] The 2025 risk factors add a full list of generative/agentic AI risks: failures, opaque or biased output, insufficient testing and controls. [3] The proxy says the full Board oversees AI matters, with the Audit and Risk Committees overseeing related controls.
